**Solution 3 is wrong.** Its claimed bound pd ≤ n fails. The code {0ⁿ, 1ⁿ} gives a polarized ideal with projective dimension 2n−2 (for quotient) or 2n−3 (for the ideal), which exceeds n for n ≥ 4 on the ideal convention and for n ≥ 3 on the quotient convention. Its single-codeword computation is correct but is not the maximum.

**Solutions 1 and 2 agree on the mathematics.** Both use the same complex Δ for C = {0ⁿ, 1ⁿ}: two simplices {x₁,…,xₙ} and {y₁,…,yₙ} joined by the n diagonal edges {xᵢ, yᵢ}. Contracting the two simplices gives n parallel edges, a wedge of n−1 circles, so H̃₁ = kⁿ⁻¹. Hochster's formula then gives pd(S/P) = 2n−2 for this code. I checked the n = 3 case independently: P is the edge ideal of a 6-cycle, and pd(S/I(C₆)) = 4 = 2n−2.

The upper bound also holds. Δ is connected for any nonempty code, so the full-vertex term contributes only at homological degree j ≥ 1. The only other large contributions come from variable-generated restrictions, which are at most n. So pd(S/P) ≤ 2n−2 for all codes.

**The disagreement is only about convention.**
- If pd(P(J_C)) means pd of the ideal itself, the answer is pd(S/P) − 1 = 2n−3 (Solution 1).
- If it means pd of the quotient R/P(J_C), the answer is 2n−2 (Solution 2).

The neural-ideal literature usually works with the quotient R/J_C, and Solution 2's 2n−2 is the cleaner statement. I am not certain which convention the source uses, so this choice carries real uncertainty. I lean toward the quotient reading and therefore Solution 2.

CHOICE: 2
